about.title: Chowchilla Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Madera County recorded a traffic death in the most recent final crash year, alongside 17 injury collisions and 27 people hurt on Chowchilla roads — numbers that don't capture what a family loses when a crash turns fatal. Corridors like SR-99, Robertson Boulevard, W Robertson Boulevard, and Trinity Avenue see a steady flow of local and pass-through traffic, and reported crashes here tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., as work and errand traffic overlaps. If you've lost a spouse, parent, or child in a Chowchilla collision, California law gives specific people the right to bring a wrongful death claim, separate from any criminal case against the at-fault driver. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect grieving families with an independent, contingency-fee attorney who can walk through eligibility, deadlines, and next steps at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Chowchilla Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing primarily to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in other circumstances. An independent attorney can help clarify where your family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Working Within the Two-Year Window
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Connecting early gives an attorney time to review the facts of the Chowchilla crash without unnecessary delay.

items.title: Recognizing What Losses Can Be Claimed
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can help your family understand which losses may apply to your specific situation.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first priority to file. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible under California law. An independent attorney can review your family's circumstances to explain where you stand.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Chowchilla?
items.answer: California generally requires wrongful death claims to be filed within two years of the date of death. If a government entity, such as a public roadway agency, may be involved given local corridors like SR-99, that deadline can be much shorter. It's worth speaking with an attorney soon rather than waiting.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they are separate matters. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action a family can pursue to seek compensation for their losses. The outcome of one doesn't determine the outcome of the other.

items.question: What kinds of compensation might our family be able to seek?
items.answer: California law allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship, guidance, and love. Every family's situation differs, so an independent attorney can walk through what may apply to yours.
